sources.reason: The central LPL account repeatedly publishes next-day BO3/BO5 starting-lineup notices with stable post permalinks. Public pages expose minute-level display times but access is inconsistent for automation, while the official CLI/API requires login and the free plan is limited to the caller's own data. No authorized response currently proves seconds-level available_at or canonical event/team/player IDs.

Individual official team accounts can publish exact five-player lineups, but a complete, versioned registry of every target team and a uniform publication contract have not been established. The same Weibo access, timestamp and identity gaps remain.

An official team account demonstrates a five-player prematch lineup and X documents seconds-level created_at via post lookup. Reading public post data through the official API requires an app and bearer token, and no complete LPL team registry or canonical event/player mapping is proven.

The 2026 LCK rulebook defines a match entry as exactly five players and says the league office discloses it after both teams arrive. The audit did not locate the official per-match public endpoint, permalink format, publication timestamp, stable identities or raw retention mechanism.

Official team accounts exist, but this audit found no repeatable, cross-team regular-season pattern proving that they publish the exact Game 1 five-player entry before T-15. Absence of indexed examples is an evidence gap, not proof that no such posts exist.

A deterministic mapping from announcement to canonical event, team and five player IDs
A versioned coverage audit showing the central feed covers the target LPL BO3/BO5 scope
Korea: The official per-match entry disclosure endpoint or channel named by LCK
